title: fix: split permission migration per alias to fit D1 CPU limit
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Migration 0046 failed on production deploy: single whole-table UPDATE ran json_valid() on all ~153k apikey rows and exceeded D1's per-query CPU limit (error 7429), rolled back cleanly (verified: 0046 unrecorded, alias counts unchanged, no partial writes).
- Rewrites 0046 as one UPDATE per alias with an instr() prefilter inside CASE so JSON functions only run on matching rows. Semantics unchanged: array order preserved, old/new pairs deduplicated, only rows whose models array contains the alias are touched.
- Migration test now runs the statements sequentially and asserts the statement count; full suite (order, dedup, edge cases, idempotence) passes unchanged.
- Adds the D1 CPU constraint to the model-management skill.

gist.headline: Aliases take the scenic route
gist.blurb: The permission garden is now tended one alias at a time instead of asking one overworked query to inspect every leaf. Same carefully preserved model permissions, with a route D1 can comfortably walk.
gist.summary: Reworked migration 0046 to canonicalize model-permission aliases with one prefiltered UPDATE per alias, avoiding D1 CPU limits while preserving array order, deduplication, and idempotence across roughly 153,000 API-key rows.
gist.impact: Production deployments can now apply the model-permission alias migration reliably, with API-key model arrays receiving the same canonical aliases without whole-table JSON processing.
gist.visual_concept: Depict permission aliases as labeled seed packets being carefully sorted into individual garden rows rather than poured into one enormous planter. Polli, wearing a tiny gardener hat and carrying a clipboard, guides a calm CRT monitor robot through a cozy database garden of API-key flowers; each row has a small, orderly alias sign, representing sequential per-alias migration work.
